tex_content.html:
Proposition
[distance zero implies isometric]

Source: petersen:page-0410 ↗ def:pet-ch11-gromov-hausdorff-distance 1. ch11:11.1.3Compact metric spaces at zero Gromov--Hausdorff distance are isometric: $\dGH (X,Y)=0$ implies that $X$ and $Y$ are isometric.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch11-gh-distance-zero-isometric \sketch Choose admissible metrics with $d_H(X,Y)<i^{-1}$, and maps $I_i:X\to Y$, $J_i:Y\to X$ moving each point by at most $i^{-1}$. Then

\[ |I_i(x_1)I_i(x_2)|\le |x_1x_2|+2i^{-1},\quad |J_i(y_1)J_i(y_2)|\le |y_1y_2|+2i^{-1}, \]

while $J_iI_i$ and $I_iJ_i$ move points by at most $2i^{-1}$. Compactness and diagonal subsequences on countable dense sets give distance-nonincreasing limits $I$ and $J$. The last estimates make them inverse, hence isometries.

□
